name: Hindi
about: Each consonant carries a built-in 'a'; vowel signs attach to it. The top line is usually drawn last.

phrases.how: स्ते joins a half स to त, plus the 'e' sign on top.
phrases.why: Greet someone in their own script on a card or a note.
phrases.dictation: Three blocks: न, म, then स्ते.

phrases.how: Vowel signs attach to consonants: वा is व plus the 'ā' sign ा.
phrases.why: Write a real thank-you card to a host or to family.
phrases.dictation: Four blocks: ध, न्य, वा, द.

phrases.how: पा is प + ा ('ā'); नी is न + ी ('ī'), drawn to the right.
phrases.why: Spot it on a menu, a sign or a bottle label.

phrases.how: The last consonant drops its built-in 'a' in speech: दोस्त is said 'dost'.
phrases.why: Sign a note to a friend. Writing it by hand helps you remember it.
phrases.dictation: Two blocks: दो, then स्त (half स joined to त).

phrases.how: ए is a vowel letter used at the start of a word; inside words vowels become signs.
phrases.why: Read quantities and order one of something off a menu.
